sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In South Liverpool, there's a neighbourhood called Granby.
sentences.zh: 在南利物浦，有一个叫格兰比的社区。

sentences.en: It used to be one of the most vibrant and diverse neighbourhoods in the UK.
sentences.zh: 它曾经是英国最有活力、最多元化的社区之一。

sentences.en: It had a busy main street lined with shops and cafes.
sentences.zh: 它曾经有一条繁忙的主街，两旁开满了商店和咖啡馆。

sentences.en: But by 2012, when an architect named Lewis Jones first visited,
sentences.zh: 但到了2012年，当一位名叫刘易斯·琼斯的建筑师第一次到访时，

sentences.en: most of the houses were unoccupied.
sentences.zh: 大部分房屋都已无人居住。

sentences.en: So, you know, a couple of hundred houses,
sentences.zh: 你知道，几百栋房子，

sentences.en: but only about 10 or 12 people still living there.
sentences.zh: 但只剩下大约10到12个人还住在那里。

sentences.en: The rest of the house is all empty.
sentences.zh: 其余的房子全都空着。

sentences.en: Granby had suffered through decades of unemployment,
sentences.zh: 格兰比经历了数十年的失业、

sentences.en: aggressive policing, and failed redevelopment schemes.
sentences.zh: 激进的警务管理和失败的重建计划。

sentences.en: And over time, the neighborhood had hollowed out.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，这个社区被掏空了。

sentences.en: That's 99PI's senior editor, Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 那是《99%隐形》的高级编辑德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: The local government had forced residents to sell their homes
sentences.zh: 当地政府强迫居民卖掉他们的房子，

sentences.en: and then boarded them up.
sentences.zh: 然后用木板封死。

sentences.en: But before the authorities sealed each house, they gutted it.
sentences.zh: 但在当局封死每一栋房子之前，他们会先将其洗劫一空。

sentences.en: They'd strip everything out.
sentences.zh: 他们会拆掉所有东西。

sentences.en: They'd strip out the copper, the lead,
sentences.zh: 他们会拆掉铜管、铅管，

sentences.en: everything that was seen to have an economic value,
sentences.zh: 所有被认为有经济价值的东西，

sentences.en: but also everything that would enable someone to live there,
sentences.zh: 以及所有能让人居住的东西，

sentences.en: the toilets, the kind of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 比如厕所和各种基础设施。

sentences.en: And that was to prevent people from squatting in those houses
sentences.zh: 这样做是为了防止人们在房子被清空后，

sentences.en: after they'd been emptied out.
sentences.zh: 非法占用这些房屋。

sentences.en: And after stripping the houses and boarding up the windows,
sentences.zh: 在拆除房屋并封死窗户后，

sentences.en: the government would place a sign on the front reading,
sentences.zh: 政府会在门前贴上一张告示，上面写着：

sentences.en: All items of value have been removed from this property.
sentences.zh: “该房产内所有有价值的物品均已被移除。”

sentences.en: And, you know, it's quite a provocation
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种相当大的挑衅，

sentences.en: when every single house on the street says on it,
sentences.zh: 当街上的每一栋房子都写着：

sentences.en: no items of value in this house.
sentences.zh: “屋内无任何有价值物品。”

sentences.en: Of course, the government meant materials like copper and lead.
sentences.zh: 当然，政府指的是铜和铅之类的材料。

sentences.en: But there are other kinds of value embedded in a home.
sentences.zh: 但房子里还蕴含着其他种类的价值。

sentences.en: There's the skill it took to build it,
sentences.zh: 比如建造它所花费的技艺，

sentences.en: and the years of life that happened inside of it,
sentences.zh: 在其中度过的岁月，

sentences.en: and the community that grew up around it.
sentences.zh: 以及围绕它成长起来的社区。

sentences.en: And what happened next in Granby would prove the signs wrong.
sentences.zh: 而接下来在格兰比发生的事情证明了这些告示是错误的。

sentences.en: A small group of residents basically refused to leave the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 一小群居民基本上拒绝离开这个社区。

sentences.en: Little by little, they began clearing trash from the empty lots,
sentences.zh: 他们一点一点地开始清理空地上的垃圾，

sentences.en: planting community gardens, and painting the boarded-up houses in bright colors.
sentences.zh: 种植社区花园，并将那些被封死的房子漆上鲜艳的颜色。

sentences.en: Eventually, this band of holdouts formed a Community Land Trust, or a CLT.
sentences.zh: 最终，这群坚守者成立了一个社区土地信托，简称CLT。

sentences.en: Their goal was to take ownership of the empty houses and bring people back to the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是获得这些空房的所有权，并让人们回到社区。

sentences.en: They raised money through a patchwork of small grants,
sentences.zh: 他们通过各种小额拨款筹集资金，

sentences.en: And then they realized it might be useful to have some folks on board who knew how to design and build stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后他们意识到，如果能有一些懂得设计和建造的人加入，可能会很有用。

sentences.en: Which is how Lewis got involved.
sentences.zh: 这就是刘易斯参与进来的方式。

sentences.en: They wanted to renovate those houses.
sentences.zh: 他们想要翻新这些房子。

sentences.en: They wanted to provide those as affordable housing.
sentences.zh: 他们想把这些房子作为经济适用房提供给人们。

sentences.en: They wanted to invite people who previously had lived in that neighborhood but had to be moved away from it.
sentences.zh: 他们想邀请那些曾经住在这个社区但被迫搬走的人，

sentences.en: They wanted to invite those people back in.
sentences.zh: 邀请这些人回来。

sentences.en: Lewis is a part of a design collective called Assemble.
sentences.zh: 刘易斯是一个名为“Assemble”的设计集体成员。

sentences.en: And with Assemble's support, the CLT advocated to the local government to stop demolishing the remaining homes.
sentences.zh: 在Assemble的支持下，CLT向当地政府游说，要求停止拆除剩余的房屋。

sentences.en: Then they worked together to renovate a handful of the old houses.
sentences.zh: 然后他们共同努力，翻新了少数几栋老房子。

sentences.en: As they pulled out materials that were too damaged to save, they started experimenting with the debris.
sentences.zh: 当他们拆除那些损坏严重无法保留的材料时，他们开始尝试利用这些废料。

sentences.en: Eventually, they set up a little backyard workshop with a local artiSt.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们和一位当地艺术家在后院建立了一个小作坊。

sentences.en: And together, they figured out how to make something that they called Granby Rock.
sentences.zh: 他们一起想出了如何制作一种他们称之为“格兰比岩”的东西。

sentences.en: And it was basically a kind of rubble terrazzo
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一种碎石水磨石，

sentences.en: that we'd take all of the broken bricks and bits of slate
sentences.zh: 我们将所有破碎的砖块和石板碎片，

sentences.en: and other kind of debris coming out of the renovation process
sentences.zh: 以及翻新过程中产生的其他碎片收集起来，

sentences.en: and we'd recast them as components for these new decorative fireplaces
sentences.zh: 然后将它们重铸成这些新的装饰性壁炉的组件，

sentences.en: and mantelpieces that we'd then put back into each house.
sentences.zh: 以及壁炉架，然后再装回每一栋房子里。

sentences.en: Every chunk of Granby rock was unique,
sentences.zh: 每一块“格兰比岩”都是独一无二的，

sentences.en: swirled with colour from the old bricks and flecked with pieces of broken slate.
sentences.zh: 旧砖块的颜色交织其中，还点缀着破碎的石板碎片。

sentences.en: Then it was poured into molds and polished smooth.
sentences.zh: 然后将其倒入模具中并打磨光滑。

sentences.en: Granby Rock fireplaces and countertops went into each of the renovated houses.
sentences.zh: “格兰比岩”壁炉和台面被安装进了每一栋翻新后的房子里。

sentences.en: It just felt important as part of kind of the process of reclaiming the narrative
sentences.zh: 这感觉很重要，作为重塑这些房子、这个社区叙事过程的一部分，

sentences.en: of these houses, of this neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 实际上，重视这里曾经存在的一切是很重要的。

sentences.en: that actually valuing everything that was there was important.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，格兰比的几十处房产被翻新，

sentences.en: Over the next few years, dozens of properties in Granby were renovated
sentences.zh: 并作为经济适用房提供出来。

sentences.en: and then offered as affordable housing.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，人们开始搬进来了。

sentences.en: And slowly, people started moving in.
sentences.zh: 新的家庭在用回收砖块制成的台面上准备晚餐。

sentences.en: New families prepared dinner on the countertops made from salvaged brick.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在用隔壁房子的废墟铸造的壁炉旁。

sentences.en: They sat near fireplaces that were cast from the rubble of the house next door.
sentences.zh: 他们以一种非常真实的方式生活着，使用的是来自社区复杂过去留下的材料。

sentences.en: They were living in a very real way, with materials from the neighborhood's complicated paSt.
sentences.zh: 在设计界，有一个术语用来描述将旧建筑的元素重新利用到新建筑中的做法。

sentences.en: In the world of design, there's a term that's used for the practice of taking elements from older buildings and reusing them in new ones.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“掠夺式建筑”（Spolia）。

sentences.en: It's called spolia.
sentences.zh: 而Assemble在格兰比所做的就是这种做法的一个版本。

sentences.en: And what Assemble did in Granby was a version of that.
sentences.zh: 设计师们审视了旧房子里的材料，他们看到了创造新事物的机会。

sentences.en: The designers looked at the materials from the old houses, and they saw an opportunity to make something new.
sentences.zh: 再利用一直是人类建造方式的一个要素。

sentences.en: Reuse has always been an element of how humans build.
sentences.zh: 我们是永无止境的回收者，从烧焦的旧木材中拔出钉子，清理并重新堆放旧砖块，把石头从一栋建筑搬运到下一栋。

sentences.en: We are endless recyclers, pulling nails out of old burned timbers and cleaning and restacking used bricks and hauling stone from one building to the next.
sentences.zh: 但对于Spolia来说，这种再利用不仅仅是实用性的问题。

sentences.en: But with Spolia, this reuse isn't just a matter of practicality.
sentences.zh: 它还承载着意义。

sentences.en: It also carries meaning.
sentences.zh: 旧材料有其历史，在新建筑中使用它，是一种承认过去依然重要的方式。

sentences.en: The old material has a history, and using it in a new building is a way of acknowledging that what came before still matters.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么Spolia会出现在世界上一些最著名的建筑中。

sentences.en: And that might be why Spolia shows up in some of the world's most famous architecture.
sentences.zh: 像圣索菲亚大教堂、巴黎圣母院和科尔多瓦清真寺这样的地方，都使用了再利用的石料。

sentences.en: Places like the Hagia Sophia, Notre Dame, and the Great Mosque of Córdoba all use repurposed stonework.
sentences.zh: 但要真正理解Spolia，你必须回到这种做法最初变得普遍的地方。

sentences.en: But to really understand Spolia, you have to go back to the place where the practice first became widespread.
sentences.zh: 它发生在文明处于生存危机之中时，它开始拆解旧世界以建立一个新世界。

sentences.en: It happened when a civilization was in the middle of an existential crisis, and it started pulling apart the old world in order to build a new one.
sentences.zh: 那个文明就是罗马帝国。

sentences.en: That civilization was the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: That's funny.
sentences.zh: 我刚才正好在想罗马帝国。

sentences.en: I was just thinking about the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 在鼎盛时期，罗马帝国控制了整个地中海世界。

sentences.en: At its peak, the Roman Empire controlled the entire Mediterranean world.
sentences.zh: 它横跨欧洲、北非和西亚。

sentences.en: It spanned Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia.
sentences.zh: 这个帝国持续了大约五个世纪。

sentences.en: The empire lasted for roughly five centuries.
sentences.zh: 近2000年后的今天，我们仍在争论它的遗产。

sentences.en: And nearly 2,000 years later, we are still arguing about its legacy.
sentences.zh: 我叫艾玛·萨瑟恩博士。

sentences.en: So my name is Dr. Emma Southern.
sentences.zh: 我是一位罗马历史学家。

sentences.en: I am a Roman historian.
sentences.zh: 我曾经是学者，现在我写书讲述罗马人有多么可怕。

sentences.en: I am an ex-academic, and now I write books about how horrible the Romans were.
sentences.zh: 艾玛喜欢憎恨罗马人。

sentences.en: Emma loves to hate the Romans.
sentences.zh: 自从她十几岁第一次了解他们以来，她就一直对此着迷。

sentences.en: She has been obsessed ever since she first learned about them as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 关于他们，我最喜欢的一点，比任何其他帝国都更甚，就是他们将自己视为最理性、

sentences.en: The thing that I love the most about them, more than any other empire really, is the complete disconnect between their image of themselves as being the most rational,
sentences.zh: 最完美、文明的巅峰、人类所能达到的最好状态的形象，与他们帝国实际的现实之间存在着完全的脱节，

sentences.en: the most perfect, the peak of civilization, the best that humanity can be, combined with the actual reality of what their empire was,
sentences.zh: 那是一个极其暴力的机器，它吞噬土地，

sentences.en: which was a horrifically violent machine that chewed up land,
sentences.zh: 它吞噬资源，并制造出大理石建筑和皇帝。

sentences.en: it chewed up resources, and produced marble buildings and emperors.
sentences.zh: 罗马人通过建筑来投射权力。

sentences.en: The Romans projected power through architecture.
sentences.zh: 皇帝们建造巨大的纪念碑来证明他们富有且合法。

sentences.en: Emperors built enormous monuments to prove that they were rich and legitimate.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都皇帝有一句名言，他说，

sentences.en: Emperor Augustus famously claimed that he, quote,
sentences.zh: 他接手时罗马是一座砖城，离开时它已是一座大理石之城。

sentences.en: found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble.
sentences.zh: 哈德良建造了万神殿。

sentences.en: Hadrian built the Pantheon.
sentences.zh: 图拉真建造了他著名的圆柱。

sentences.en: Trajan built his famous column.
sentences.zh: 弗拉维王朝的皇帝们建造了斗兽场。

sentences.en: The Flavian emperors made the Colosseum.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们今天熟悉的所有罗马皇帝，

sentences.en: In fact, pretty much all the Roman emperors that we're familiar with today
sentences.zh: 几乎都是那些留下了某种纪念性建筑的人。

sentences.en: are the ones who left behind something monumental.
sentences.zh: 因为这正是最初建造这些纪念碑的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: Because that was the whole point of building the monuments in the first place.
sentences.zh: 罗马人总是着眼于未来。

sentences.en: The Romans were always thinking about the future.
sentences.zh: 他们总是想象着我们，在2000年后的今天，

sentences.en: They were always imagining us, 2,000 years down the road,
sentences.zh: 惊叹于他们所创造的一切。

sentences.en: marveling at what they've created.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们有能力建造昂贵的石头建筑，

sentences.en: As soon as they can afford to build an expensive stone,
sentences.zh: 他们就会建造，因为他们知道它会持久，

sentences.en: they do build an expensive stone because they know it will last
sentences.zh: 而且他们总是为未来的几代人着想，

sentences.en: and they're always producing for the generations in the future
sentences.zh: 以确保他们会被铭记。

sentences.en: to make sure they will be remembered.
sentences.zh: 最昂贵、耐用、具有纪念意义的建筑石材是大理石，

sentences.en: The most expensive, durable, monumental stone to build with was marble
sentences.zh: 罗马人从帝国的各个角落开采它。

sentences.en: and Romans quarried it from all over their empire.
sentences.zh: 他们从希腊获取绿色大理石，从埃及获取红色斑岩。

sentences.en: They got green marble from Greece and red porphyry from Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这些罗马采石场是国有的，主要依靠奴隶劳动。

sentences.en: These Roman quarries were state-owned and they relied mostly on slave labor.
sentences.zh: 它们位于炎热干燥的地方，全部由军队监管。

sentences.en: They were located in hot, dry places, and they were all overseen by the army.
sentences.zh: 那是极其可怕、令人筋疲力尽的工作。

sentences.en: It was terrible, back-breaking work.
sentences.zh: 开采大理石后，罗马人将其运过地中海，

sentences.en: After mining the marble, the Romans shipped it across the Mediterranean
sentences.zh: 并用它建造了他们赖以成名的宏伟建筑。

sentences.en: and used it to build the kind of magnificent structures they became famous for.
sentences.zh: 这就是几个世纪以来的情况。

sentences.en: And that's how it went for many centuries.
sentences.zh: 罗马人建造纪念碑来展示他们有多么了不起，

sentences.en: The Romans built monuments to show how awesome they were,
sentences.zh: 使用来自遥远地方的稀有石材，传达的信息很明确。

sentences.en: using rare stone from far-flung places, and the message it conveyed was clear.
sentences.zh: 罗马是永恒的。

sentences.en: Rome was eternal.
sentences.zh: 直到它不再是为止。

sentences.en: Until it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 从公元3世纪中叶开始，

sentences.en: Starting around the middle of the 3rd century,
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国遭遇了一系列相互叠加的灾难。

sentences.en: the Roman Empire got hit by a series of overlapping catastrophes.
sentences.zh: 每一个灾难都让下一个变得更糟。

sentences.en: Each one made the next one worse.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全是罗马的灭亡。

sentences.en: This wasn't exactly the fall of Rome.
sentences.zh: 这更像是它的踉跄。

sentences.en: It was more like the stumble.
sentences.zh: 首先是政治混乱。

sentences.en: First, there was political chaos.
sentences.zh: 人们不断谋杀皇帝，然后宣布自己为皇帝，

sentences.en: People keep murdering the emperor and then declaring themselves emperor
sentences.zh: 地点远在罗马之外，

sentences.en: far, far away from Rome.
sentences.zh: 这非常混乱，高层没有任何稳定性。

sentences.en: and it's very chaotic and there's no stability at the top.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，帝国的邻居们正在观察这种政治不稳定，

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the empire's neighbors were watching this political instability
sentences.zh: 他们心想，嘿，机会来了。

sentences.en: and they're thinking, hey, there's an opportunity here.
sentences.zh: 帝国周围的所有人都认为这是一个绝佳的时机，

sentences.en: Everybody around the outside of the empire thinks this is a great time
sentences.zh: 试图去尝试为自己夺取一些土地。

sentences.en: to try and have a go at taking some land for themselves.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到非罗马民族试图进入帝国境内。

sentences.en: You start to get non-Roman peoples trying to get inside the empire.
sentences.zh: 然后一场大流行病袭来。

sentences.en: Then a pandemic hit.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“西普里安瘟疫”，非常可怕。

sentences.en: It was called the Plague of the Cyprian and it was horrific.
sentences.zh: 在近20年的时间里，它席卷了整个帝国。

sentences.en: For almost 20 years, it ripped through the empire.
sentences.zh: 一些学者现在认为这是一种类似于埃博拉的病毒。

sentences.en: Some scholars now think it was a virus similar to Ebola.
sentences.zh: 它在20年的时间里，以季节性周期，每天夺走数千人的生命。

sentences.en: And it was killing thousands of people a day for 20 years in seasonal cycles.
sentences.zh: 这就是99%隐形。

sentences.en: And then the climate was also changing.
sentences.zh: 随后气候也发生了变化。

sentences.en: The agricultural parts of the empire experienced terrible droughts.
sentences.zh: 帝国境内的农业区遭遇了严重的干旱。

sentences.en: The Nile stopped flooding.
sentences.zh: 尼罗河停止了泛滥。

sentences.en: Crops failed.
sentences.zh: 农作物歉收。

sentences.en: People starved.
sentences.zh: 人们陷入饥荒。

sentences.en: Oh, and then there was hyperinflation on top of everything else.
sentences.zh: 哦，而且在那之上还出现了恶性通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And these various crises went on and on for decades.
sentences.zh: 这些各种各样的危机持续了几十年之久。

sentences.en: Needless to say, nobody was really looking after the Romans' magnificent marble buildings
sentences.zh: 不用说，在那半个世纪的混乱不堪中，

sentences.en: during this absolute clusterf**k of a half century.
sentences.zh: 根本没人去照看罗马人那些宏伟的大理石建筑。

sentences.en: There was a lot of deferred maintenance,
sentences.zh: 大量的维护工作被搁置了，

sentences.en: while people dealt with hemorrhagic fevers and famine and invasion from all sides.
sentences.zh: 而人们正忙于应对出血热、饥荒以及四面八方的入侵。

sentences.en: Nobody has been replacing broken tiles or polishing the tiled floors
sentences.zh: 没人去更换破损的瓷砖，也没人去打磨地砖，

sentences.en: or putting the mosaics back together.
sentences.zh: 更没人去修复那些马赛克拼贴画。

sentences.en: The result was that in Rome, there was a lot of beautiful, expensive marble just sitting there, slowly falling apart from neglect.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，在罗马，许多精美昂贵的大理石就那样闲置着，因疏于照管而慢慢损毁。

sentences.en: At the same time that was happening, Rome's quarries in Greece, Egypt, and North Africa were becoming really hard to access.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，罗马在希腊、埃及和北非的采石场也变得极难进入。

sentences.en: Travel and trade was much more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 旅行和贸易变得危险得多。

sentences.en: That meant if you wanted to build something impressive, and the Romans always did, you couldn't just order up some new marble.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你想建造宏伟的建筑——而罗马人向来如此——你无法直接订购新的大理石。

sentences.en: The Romans were in a bind.
sentences.zh: 罗马人陷入了困境。

sentences.en: Their colossal old monuments were falling down and they couldn't get the material to build new ones.
sentences.zh: 他们那些巨大的古老纪念碑正在倒塌，而他们却无法获得建造新建筑的材料。

sentences.en: Until finally one guy connected the dots.
sentences.zh: 直到最后，有一个人把这些点串联了起来。

sentences.en: He realized that you could use those old buildings as raw material to build new stuff.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，你可以利用那些旧建筑作为原材料来建造新东西。

sentences.en: His name was Constantine.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫君士坦丁。

sentences.en: By the time Constantine kind of comes and unites the empire, everybody is very ready for a savior.
sentences.zh: 当君士坦丁出现并统一帝国时，每个人都非常渴望一位救世主。

sentences.en: Constantine grew up a soldier, and he spent nearly 20 years fighting one civil war after another until finally he controlled the entire empire.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁成长于军旅，他花了近20年时间打了一场又一场内战，直到最终控制了整个帝国。

sentences.en: Then he proceeded to transform it.
sentences.zh: 随后，他着手对帝国进行改造。

sentences.en: He legalized Christianity, for one thing, and most relevant to our story, he launched an enormous wave of construction.
sentences.zh: 首先，他使基督教合法化；而与我们故事最相关的是，他掀起了一场巨大的建设浪潮。

sentences.en: Like every emperor before him, he understood the power of architecture.
sentences.zh: 像他之前的每一位皇帝一样，他深谙建筑的力量。

sentences.en: And so did the people around him.
sentences.zh: 他周围的人也一样。

sentences.en: Not long after his bloody ascent to power, the Roman Senate gave him a gift, a huge triumphal arch right next to the Colosseum.
sentences.zh: 在他血腥夺权后不久，罗马元老院送给他一份礼物：一座紧邻斗兽场的巨大凯旋门。

sentences.en: I have Constantine's arch tattooed on me because it's the quintessential arch.
sentences.zh: 我身上纹着君士坦丁凯旋门，因为它就是凯旋门的典范。

sentences.en: The monument was officially a celebration of Constantine's rule.
sentences.zh: 这座纪念碑名义上是为了庆祝君士坦丁的统治。

sentences.en: But Emma says the Senate had its own more self-interested reasons for building the big, beautiful arch.
sentences.zh: 但艾玛说，元老院建造这座宏伟美丽拱门的原因，更多是出于自身的利益考量。

sentences.en: Which is the kind of thing you do when you have an emperor who kills a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 当你面对一位杀人如麻的皇帝时，你就会做这种事。

sentences.en: You give him the biggest arch, you give him anything that will make him happy and hopefully not turn his really big successful army against you at any point.
sentences.zh: 你会送他最大的拱门，送他任何能让他高兴的东西，并祈祷他不会在某个时刻让那支庞大且战功赫赫的军队掉转枪口对准你。

sentences.en: The arch was covered in panels with sculpted scenes on them, but many of those panels weren't originally made for Constantine.
sentences.zh: 拱门上覆盖着刻有场景的面板，但其中许多面板最初并非为君士坦丁所制。

sentences.en: They were taken from monuments honoring emperors who'd lived around 200 years before.
sentences.zh: 它们取自纪念约200年前皇帝们的古迹。

sentences.en: This was partly a matter of practicality, because it was hard to get enough new marble to make the arch from scratch.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上是出于实用考虑，因为很难获得足够的新大理石来从头建造这座拱门。

sentences.en: But maybe more importantly, it was a symbolic move.
sentences.zh: 但或许更重要的是，这是一个象征性的举动。

sentences.en: Because in a narcissistic twist, the images of the old emperors had been reworked to look like Constantine.
sentences.zh: 因为在一种自恋的扭曲下，旧皇帝的形象被重新加工，看起来像君士坦丁。

sentences.en: A sculptor has gone in and subtly reshaped the face, because he's got quite a distinctive head, Constantine.
sentences.zh: 雕刻家介入并巧妙地重塑了面部，因为君士坦丁的头部特征非常鲜明。

sentences.en: So they have made his big square head and put that onto the original.
sentences.zh: 所以他们制作了他那硕大的方形脑袋，并将其安到了原有的雕像上。

sentences.en: This effectively made it look like Constantine, with his big square head, was doing all the stuff that past emperors had done.
sentences.zh: 这有效地营造出一种假象，仿佛长着大方脑袋的君士坦丁完成了过去皇帝们所做的一切。

sentences.en: Like riding a horse over the bodies of his enemies, or addressing a crowd of troops, or hunting a lion.
sentences.zh: 比如骑马踏过敌人的尸体，向军队发表讲话，或是猎狮。

sentences.en: The idea was to remind people of when Rome was great.
sentences.zh: 其目的是提醒人们罗马曾经的伟大。

sentences.en: to evoke a memory of Rome at its healthiest, at its most prosperous.
sentences.zh: 唤起人们对罗马最鼎盛、最繁荣时期的记忆。

sentences.en: So it is a specific and deliberate choice to make that clear connection
sentences.zh: 因此，做出这种明确的联系是一个具体且深思熟虑的选择，

sentences.en: back to a kind of lost golden paSt.
sentences.zh: 旨在回溯某种失落的黄金时代。

sentences.en: Constantine's arch was a masterpiece of political messaging,
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁凯旋门是政治宣传的杰作，

sentences.en: and it was also a turning point in the history of architectural reuse.
sentences.zh: 它也是建筑再利用历史上的一个转折点。

sentences.en: There has been some debate among scholars about whether the repurposing of the panels
sentences.zh: 学者们对于这种面板的再利用究竟是出于艺术目的还是纯粹的实用主义，一直存在争议，但许多人认为这不仅仅是为了削减成本的回收利用。

sentences.en: was artistic or just practical, but a lot of them think it wasn't just recycling to cut costs.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了削减成本的回收利用。

sentences.en: It was meant to communicate something about the new political moment.
sentences.zh: 它旨在传达关于新政治时刻的某种信息。

sentences.en: A column pulled out of a pagan temple still has an aura of prestige.
sentences.zh: 从异教神庙中拆下的圆柱依然带有某种威望的光环。

sentences.en: A carved panel from Rome's
sentences.zh: 来自罗马黄金时代的雕刻面板，

sentences.en: golden age still carries a certain authority.
sentences.zh: 依然承载着某种权威。

sentences.en: Constantine understood that if you place those
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁明白，如果你将这些材料置于新的语境中，

sentences.en: materials in a new context, all of that accumulated meaning could be deployed in new ways.
sentences.zh: 所有积累的意义都可以以新的方式被调用。

sentences.en: It was reuse as propaganda.
sentences.zh: 这就是作为政治宣传的再利用。

sentences.en: Constantine's reuse also set a new precedent.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁的再利用也开创了一个新的先例。

sentences.en: Once the emperor himself started pulling apart old monuments to build new ones,
sentences.zh: 一旦皇帝本人开始拆除旧古迹来建造新建筑，

sentences.en: it gave permission to the rest of the empire.
sentences.zh: 这就给了帝国其余部分许可。

sentences.en: It became this interesting and legitimate thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一件有趣且合情合理的事情。

sentences.en: And soon this kind of reuse was spreading.
sentences.zh: 很快，这种再利用方式就开始蔓延开来。

sentences.en: People started salvaging old columns and decorative friezes and ornamental stonework.
sentences.zh: 人们开始打捞旧圆柱、装饰性檐口和装饰性石雕。

sentences.en: They would pull that material out of old buildings and use it in new construction.
sentences.zh: 他们会从旧建筑中拆除这些材料，并将其用于新的建筑中。

sentences.en: And a lot of that new construction was churches.
sentences.zh: 而许多这类新建筑都是教堂。

sentences.en: Constantine had legalized Christianity, and now the faith needed a lot of grand new buildings to match its status as a legitimate religion.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁使基督教合法化，现在这种信仰需要大量宏伟的新建筑来匹配其作为合法宗教的地位。

sentences.en: Huge basilicas went up across the empire, and they needed marble.
sentences.zh: 巨大的巴西利卡式教堂在帝国各地拔地而起，而它们需要大理石。

sentences.en: Thankfully, there were crumbling pagan temples everywhere,
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，到处都是摇摇欲坠的异教神庙，

sentences.en: full of the kinds of stone that would make churches look amazing.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了能让教堂看起来美轮美奂的石材。

sentences.en: And it becomes about the power of the church on earth to show that this is God's earth
sentences.zh: 这变成了关于教会在这片土地上的权力，以展示这是上帝的土地，

sentences.en: and we can decorate his house with all of the beautiful things.
sentences.zh: 我们可以用所有美好的事物来装饰他的居所。

sentences.en: The other thing that supercharged this new wave of architectural reuse
sentences.zh: 推动这股新建筑再利用浪潮的另一件事，

sentences.en: was that Constantine had founded a new capital named for himself in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 是君士坦丁在君士坦丁堡建立了一座以自己名字命名的新首都。

sentences.en: And much of the new building in Constantinople involved materials salvaged from other places.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁堡的大部分新建筑都涉及从其他地方打捞来的材料。

sentences.en: When he founds Constantinople, he sweeps around the empire taking up cool stuff from other places,
sentences.zh: 当他建立君士坦丁堡时，他横扫帝国，从其他地方搜罗酷炫的东西，

sentences.en: basically, in order to decorate his new city, much to the stress of everybody else.
sentences.zh: 基本上是为了装饰他的新城市，这让其他人倍感压力。

sentences.en: A lot of people were not thrilled about the old marble temples being pulled apart.
sentences.zh: 许多人对旧大理石神庙被拆毁感到非常不满。

sentences.en: Especially in Rome, it sometimes felt like the city was being taken apart piece by piece.
sentences.zh: 特别是在罗马，有时感觉这座城市正在被一点一点地拆解。

sentences.en: Everything that we know about what ordinary people saw about it is that they hated it.
sentences.zh: 我们所了解的关于普通民众对此的看法是，他们对此深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: People actually rioted.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至发生了暴乱。

sentences.en: They were so fed up that their neighborhoods were starting to look ramshackle and just bad.
sentences.zh: 他们受够了自己居住的街区开始变得破烂不堪，甚至糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Like, that was a nice building that was in my neighborhood, and it had really nice columns on it.
sentences.zh: 比如，那曾是我街区里的一座漂亮建筑，上面有非常精美的圆柱。

sentences.en: And now it doesn't have any columns, and the roof is falling down.
sentences.zh: 而现在它连一根圆柱都没有了，屋顶也正在倒塌。

sentences.en: And what, nobody's going to do anything about that.
sentences.zh: 怎么，难道没人管管吗？

sentences.en: They needed the equivalent of a Roman HOA, some enforcer who might keep up the standards of the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们需要一个类似罗马业主委员会的组织，一些能够维持街区标准的执法者。

sentences.en: And eventually, about 50 years after Constantine basically invented this kind of reuse, later emperors were passing laws trying to stop it.
sentences.zh: 最终，在君士坦丁基本发明这种再利用方式约50年后，后来的皇帝们开始颁布法律试图阻止它。

sentences.en: If you were caught stealing stone from buildings, you could be fined.
sentences.zh: 如果你被抓到从建筑上偷窃石材，你可能会被罚款。

sentences.en: But the laws were pretty toothless, and it kept happening anyway.
sentences.zh: 但这些法律几乎毫无约束力，这种事依然不断发生。

sentences.en: And this tension never really went away.
sentences.zh: 这种张力从未真正消失。

sentences.en: There were the people who wanted to preserve the old buildings.
sentences.zh: 有一群人想要保护旧建筑，

sentences.en: And then there were the people who wanted to strip them for parts.
sentences.zh: 而另一群人则想把它们拆解变卖。

sentences.en: In fact, that tension eventually became embedded in the word that we use for the practice.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种张力最终被嵌入了我们用来描述这种做法的词汇中。

sentences.en: The term spolia was coined during the Renaissance,
sentences.zh: “Spolia”（战利品）一词是在文艺复兴时期创造的，

sentences.en: when researchers of the time had rediscovered classical Rome and fallen in love with it.
sentences.zh: 当时的研究人员重新发现了古典罗马并爱上了它。

sentences.en: And when they noticed that beautiful ancient Roman stonework had been salvaged
sentences.zh: 当他们注意到精美的古罗马石雕被回收，

sentences.en: and then wedged into medieval church walls, they were disgusted.
sentences.zh: 并被塞进中世纪教堂的墙壁时，他们感到厌恶。

sentences.en: It looked to them like the church had pillaged the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这就像是教会洗劫了古代世界。

sentences.en: They coined the word spolia from the Latin for the spoils of war.
sentences.zh: 他们从拉丁语中创造了“spolia”一词，意为战争的战利品。

sentences.en: To describe this process, to make it into a process of war, of almost attack on these old buildings.
sentences.zh: 用来描述这个过程，将其变成一个战争的过程，几乎是对这些古老建筑的攻击。

sentences.en: The use of spolia starts as a renaissance moral judgment on what has happened.
sentences.zh: “Spolia”的使用最初是对所发生事件的一种文艺复兴式的道德评判。

sentences.en: But over time, the term lost its moral sting.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，这个词失去了它的道德刺痛感。

sentences.en: And now in academic writing, it is just used as a neutral descriptor.
sentences.zh: 现在在学术写作中，它仅被用作一个中性的描述词。

sentences.en: Spolia outlived the empire that made it famous.
sentences.zh: “Spolia”的生命力比让它成名的帝国还要长久。

sentences.en: Wherever the Romans built stuff, later civilizations found their materials and put them to new uses.
sentences.zh: 无论罗马人在哪里建造建筑，后来的文明都会找到他们的材料并赋予其新的用途。

sentences.en: Roman tiles showed up in medieval churches in England.
sentences.zh: 罗马瓷砖出现在了英国的中世纪教堂里。

sentences.en: Charlemagne installed Roman stonework in the chapel in his palace.
sentences.zh: 查理曼大帝在他的宫殿礼拜堂中安装了罗马石雕。

sentences.en: And across the Islamic world, mosques were built with columns salvaged from Roman temples.
sentences.zh: 在整个伊斯兰世界，清真寺也是用从罗马神庙中打捞出来的圆柱建造的。

sentences.en: But spolia is really just one expression of a much older and more universal human instinct to reuse.
sentences.zh: 但“spolia”实际上只是人类更古老、更普遍的再利用本能的一种表现。

sentences.en: After the Second World War, for example, when European cities lay in ruins, people picked through the rubble and used what they found to rebuild.
sentences.zh: 例如，第二次世界大战后，当欧洲城市沦为废墟时，人们在瓦砾中搜寻，并利用他们找到的东西进行重建。

sentences.en: That wasn't really spolia, because it wasn't about symbolism.
sentences.zh: 那并不完全是“spolia”，因为它不涉及象征意义。

sentences.en: It was just necessity.
sentences.zh: 那仅仅是出于必要。

sentences.en: But still, the underlying logic was the same.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，其潜在的逻辑是一样的。

sentences.en: For most of human history, reuse wasn't some special thing.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，再利用并不是什么特殊的事情。

sentences.en: It was just how people built.
sentences.zh: 这只是人们建造的方式。

sentences.en: But it's not how people build anymore.
sentences.zh: 但现在人们不再这样建造了。

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们回归的地方。

sentences.en: Today, the vast majority of construction involves demolishing what's already there and starting from scratch,
sentences.zh: 今天，绝大多数建筑工程都涉及拆除现有建筑并从零开始，

sentences.en: with all new materials that are uniform and predictable, with no history and no variability.
sentences.zh: 使用全新的、统一且可预测的材料，没有历史，也没有差异性。

sentences.en: It's often cheaper and more efficient than reusing the old stuff.
sentences.zh: 这通常比再利用旧材料更便宜、更高效。

sentences.en: But now, a growing number of architects and researchers think that reuse is a practice we need to relearn.
sentences.zh: 但现在，越来越多的建筑师和研究人员认为，再利用是我们必须重新学习的实践。

sentences.en: Because it turns out that making everything from scratch, with raw materials, is something the planet can't sustain.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，用原材料从头制造一切，是地球无法承受的。

sentences.en: As we look into the future, we're not going to be in an extract-and-throw-away world.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，我们将不再处于一个“开采-丢弃”的世界。

sentences.en: This is Kate Simanen, a professor of architecture at the University of Washington.
sentences.zh: 这是华盛顿大学建筑学教授凯特·西曼恩。

sentences.en: I mean, by requirement, we're going to need to reuse the things that we have made previously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，出于必要，我们将需要再利用我们之前制造的东西。

sentences.en: Otherwise, ultimately, we would run out.
sentences.zh: 否则，最终我们会耗尽资源。

sentences.en: The labor and fuel expended in creating even a single brick are enormous.
sentences.zh: 即使是制造一块砖所消耗的劳动力和燃料也是巨大的。

sentences.en: And Kate says that it's worth sitting with what it actually takes to make something new.
sentences.zh: 凯特说，值得深思一下制造新东西到底需要付出什么代价。

sentences.en: So in order to make a brick, you have to excavate the clay material from the earth.
sentences.zh: 为了制造一块砖，你必须从地球上挖掘粘土材料。

sentences.en: And in doing that, you're using an excavator that's burning diesel.
sentences.zh: 在挖掘过程中，你使用的是燃烧柴油的挖掘机。

sentences.en: And so as you're burning that diesel, emissions go up into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 当你燃烧柴油时，排放物就会进入大气层。

sentences.en: So that's step one, just digging the clay out of the ground.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一步，仅仅是把粘土从地里挖出来。

sentences.en: Then you have to shape it.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须塑造它。

sentences.en: And that's often done with a machine.
sentences.zh: 这通常是用机器完成的。

sentences.en: And that machine might be using electricity, making that electricity has emissions.
sentences.zh: 而那台机器可能在使用电力，产生电力就会有排放。

sentences.en: Then the brick needs to be cured.
sentences.zh: 然后砖块需要固化。

sentences.en: And that usually means burning natural gas to fire the kiln.
sentences.zh: 这通常意味着燃烧天然气来加热窑炉。

sentences.en: And that natural gas then releases emissions into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 而天然气随后会将排放物释放到大气中。

sentences.en: And finally, you have to transport the brick to wherever it's needed,
sentences.zh: 最后，你必须将砖块运输到需要的地方，

sentences.en: which requires a truck or a train or an airplane.
sentences.zh: 这需要卡车、火车或飞机。

sentences.en: And that then is also, again, likely burning diesel, which releases emissions.
sentences.zh: 而这通常也可能是在燃烧柴油，从而释放排放物。

sentences.en: Now consider every brick, every steel beam, every panel of drywall,
sentences.zh: 现在考虑一下每一块砖、每一根钢梁、每一块干墙板，

sentences.en: and every pane of glass in every building in the world.
sentences.zh: 以及世界上每一栋建筑中的每一块玻璃。

sentences.en: There's just an enormous amount of materials and labor
sentences.zh: 建筑环境中存在着巨大的材料和劳动力投入，

sentences.en: and what's called embodied carbon in the built environment.
sentences.zh: 以及所谓的“隐含碳”。

sentences.en: Which is why a growing number of architects and engineers
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么越来越多的建筑师和工程师

sentences.en: argue that we basically need to practice spolia at scale.
sentences.zh: 主张我们基本上需要大规模地实践“spolia”。

sentences.en: And that sounds like a great idea,
sentences.zh: 这听起来是个好主意，

sentences.en: but it's actually very hard to do.
sentences.zh: 但实际上很难做到。

sentences.en: When you salvage something like an old steel beam,
sentences.zh: 当你打捞像旧钢梁这样的东西时，

sentences.en: it's hard to know exactly what you've got, like what it's actually made of and what loads it can
sentences.zh: 很难确切知道你手头有什么，比如它到底是什么材质，能承受什么负荷

sentences.en: carry.
sentences.zh: 运送。

sentences.en: There is no reliable supply chain for reclaimed materials, at least not at the scale
sentences.zh: 回收材料没有可靠的供应链，至少达不到我们真正需要的规模

sentences.en: we really need.
sentences.zh: 应付

sentences.en: And most buildings aren't designed to be taken apart.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数建筑在设计时并没有考虑拆解。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of time and
sentences.zh: 拆解旧建筑需要耗费大量的时间和

sentences.en: effort to deconstruct an old building piece by piece so that the parts can be used again.
sentences.zh: 精力，才能将建筑逐块拆除，以便再次利用这些部件。

sentences.en: How we make buildings today has influence on how easy they will be to take apart
sentences.zh: 我们今天建造建筑的方式，影响着它们在未来

sentences.en: in the future.
sentences.zh: 拆解的难易程度。

sentences.en: And not that many building owners today are asking their design teams to make it
sentences.zh: 如今并没有多少业主会要求设计团队考虑

sentences.en: easy to tear down my building in 60 to 80 years.
sentences.zh: 如何让我的建筑在60到80年后易于拆除。

sentences.en: That's not really their top priority.
sentences.zh: 那并不是他们的首要任务。

sentences.en: In other words, it's hard to get out of that emperor mindset that buildings must last forever.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，很难摆脱那种建筑必须永垂不朽的“帝王心态”。

sentences.en: There are some traditions that better understand a building's transience.
sentences.zh: 有些传统能更好地理解建筑的短暂性。

sentences.en: For example, Japanese temples used to be built without nails or screws.
sentences.zh: 例如，日本寺庙过去建造时是不使用钉子或螺丝的。

sentences.en: Instead, they were supported by interlocking wooden joints so that they could be taken apart and reassembled.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们由互锁的木接头支撑，因此可以拆卸并重新组装。

sentences.en: And there are modern examples too, like the Olympic Village during the 2024 Paris Games
sentences.zh: 现代也有这样的例子，比如2024年巴黎奥运会的奥运村，

sentences.en: that was designed to be converted to housing after the competition.
sentences.zh: 其设计初衷就是在比赛结束后改建为住宅。

sentences.en: So there are buildings, here and there, being designed with their next life in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，到处都有建筑在设计时就考虑到了它们的下一段生命。

sentences.en: I asked Kate what she thought about the Roman connection,
sentences.zh: 我问凯特她对罗马式联系的看法，

sentences.en: how they took their crumbling buildings and used them as raw materials for something new.
sentences.zh: 关于他们如何将摇摇欲坠的建筑作为新建筑的原材料。

sentences.en: I think those buildings actually had fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些建筑实际上已经倒塌了。

sentences.en: You know, they were the debris of previous civilizations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们是前代文明的残骸。

sentences.en: And so ultimately, our lives will be the debris for other civilizations.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，我们的生活也将成为其他文明的残骸。

sentences.en: There are a lot of ways to think about what makes building materials valuable.
sentences.zh: 关于建筑材料的价值，有很多种思考方式。

sentences.en: Kate thinks about it in terms of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 凯特是从稀缺性的角度来考虑的。

sentences.en: The earth is finite.
sentences.zh: 地球资源是有限的。

sentences.en: There's not an endless amount of clay, sand, and stone.
sentences.zh: 粘土、沙子和石头并不是取之不尽的。

sentences.en: We have to be careful not to exhaust the materials we have.
sentences.zh: 我们必须小心，不要耗尽我们现有的材料。

sentences.en: The Roman emperors thought about value in terms of prestige.
sentences.zh: 罗马皇帝从威望的角度来衡量价值。

sentences.en: Placing old materials in new contexts
sentences.zh: 将旧材料置于新的语境中，

sentences.en: allowed them to communicate something about continuity and power.
sentences.zh: 让他们能够传达出某种关于连续性和权力的信息。

sentences.en: And the residents of Granby in South Liverpool measured value in a different way.
sentences.zh: 而南利物浦格兰比的居民则以不同的方式衡量价值。

sentences.en: They cared about the history of their neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们关心自己社区的历史。

sentences.en: And when they worked with Lewis Jones and the team at Assemble,
sentences.zh: 当他们与刘易斯·琼斯和Assemble团队合作时，

sentences.en: they didn't just see old and dilapidated houses.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的不仅仅是破旧的房屋。

sentences.en: They saw the raw materials for something new.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了新事物的原材料。

sentences.en: Granby Rock, the product they made from the neighborhood's debris,
sentences.zh: “格兰比之石”，即他们用社区残骸制成的产品，

sentences.en: was a way of insisting that the community still had worth.
sentences.zh: 是一种坚持社区依然有价值的方式。

sentences.en: It was important to put these things into the houses
sentences.zh: 将这些东西放入房屋中很重要，

sentences.en: that would express the, you know, yeah, love and care and attention that had gone into renovating
sentences.zh: 因为这能表达出，你知道，那种在翻新过程中投入的爱、关怀和心血，

sentences.en: them.
sentences.zh: 在

sentences.en: But since the early days of the Granby project, Lewis and his collaborators have
sentences.zh: 但自格兰比项目初期以来，刘易斯和他的合作者们

sentences.en: started thinking much more about reuse in the context of climate change.
sentences.zh: 开始更多地从气候变化的背景下思考再利用问题。

sentences.en: The Granby workshop
sentences.zh: 格兰比工作室

sentences.en: didn't close when the renovation was finished.
sentences.zh: 并没有在翻新完成后关闭。

sentences.en: Instead, it grew into something bigger,
sentences.zh: 相反，它发展成了更大的规模，

sentences.en: a manufacturing studio in the neighborhood that's still running today.
sentences.zh: 一个至今仍在运营的社区制造工作室。

sentences.en: It produces architectural
sentences.zh: 它利用回收材料生产建筑

sentences.en: tiles and ceramics out of recycled materials.
sentences.zh: 瓷砖和陶瓷。

sentences.en: They fire these tiles at lower temperatures to
sentences.zh: 他们以较低的温度烧制这些瓷砖，以

sentences.en: reduce their environmental footprint, and they use electric kilns.
sentences.zh: 减少环境足迹，并且他们使用电窑。

sentences.en: So what started as spolia in the
sentences.zh: 所以，最初意义上的“掠夺性建筑材料”（spolia）

sentences.en: oldest sense has evolved into something more like what Kate Simenon advocates for.
sentences.zh: 已经演变成了更接近凯特·西蒙农所倡导的东西。

sentences.en: The workshop now
sentences.zh: 工作室现在

sentences.en: helps other projects turn their construction debris into new building materials.
sentences.zh: 帮助其他项目将建筑垃圾转化为新的建筑材料。

sentences.en: It's reuse that
sentences.zh: 这是一种涉及象征意义的再利用，

sentences.en: involves symbolism, but it's also a practical recognition that we can't keep extracting raw
sentences.zh: 但也是一种务实的认识，即我们不能永远开采原材料。

sentences.en: materials forever.
sentences.zh: 永远的材料。

sentences.en: Every project always starts with trying to understand what's already there
sentences.zh: 每个项目总是从试图了解现有的东西开始，

sentences.en: and how to be really like resourceful.
sentences.zh: 以及如何真正做到足智多谋。

sentences.en: And so reuse is a big, big part of that.
sentences.zh: 所以再利用是其中非常、非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: I asked Lewis what Granby looks like today, more than a decade after Semble joined with
sentences.zh: 我问刘易斯今天的格兰比是什么样子，在Assemble加入

sentences.en: the Community Land Trust to renovate the first houses.
sentences.zh: 社区土地信托翻新第一批房屋十多年后。

sentences.en: Granby today still very much has the same spirit.
sentences.zh: 今天的格兰比依然保留着同样的精神。

sentences.en: I think it had, you know, when I first visited 15 odd years ago, there's still a kind of
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，当我15年前第一次访问时，那里仍然有一种

sentences.en: sense of wildness there.
sentences.zh: 荒野感。

sentences.en: You know, there's still like furniture on the street, there's plants in the pavement,
sentences.zh: 你知道，街上还有家具，人行道上有植物，

sentences.en: there's the odd painting on the wall, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 墙上偶尔有画，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But obviously, you know, amongst that, there are a lot more people living now.
sentences.zh: 但显然，你知道，在这些之中，现在住着更多的人。

sentences.en: Lewis described kids playing on the streets,
sentences.zh: 刘易斯描述了孩子们在街上玩耍的场景，

sentences.en: where not too long ago every house had one of those signs,
sentences.zh: 而在不久前，每栋房子都挂着那种牌子，

sentences.en: the ones that said,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，

sentences.en: all items of value have been removed from this property.
sentences.zh: 该房产内所有有价值的物品已被移走。

sentences.en: Those signs were, of course, wrong.
sentences.zh: 那些牌子当然是错的。

sentences.en: The materials of the past are never worthless.
sentences.zh: 过去的材料永远不会毫无价值。
